method: BASELINE, a layer beside baseline-2026-10 (untouched). Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE (open questions answer NOTHING, asserted, with a fork register); the s 197(1) and s 193(b) deadlines are regulative rules run by EVALTRACE inside the questions; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Social Security (Administration) Act 1999, Compilation No. 163, compilation date 5 December 2025, includes amendments up to Act No. 73, 2025 (register id C2026C00010, in 2 volumes), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A00580.txt. No instrument needed. Debts (existence, amount, recovery, write-off, waiver) are the Social Security Act 1991's Chapter 5, not encoded.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run ssaa-overpayment-dates.l4 ; l4 run ssaa-overpayment.l4 ; l4 run ssaa-cases-overpayment.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

focus: overpayment and debt disputes (the income-averaging debt episode): computer decisions, notice, information notices, offences, ART settlement
scope: From the seat of the person paid: ss 6A, 236 (computer decisions in writing, the Secretary's); s 83 (computer changes as determinations, and their day); s 237 (the day notice of a decision is given); Part 5 Division 1: ss 191A, 192 (all paragraphs), 193, 194, 195(2), (4)-(6), 196, 197, 197A, 197B, 198(2); s 166(3) (s 191A off when the Secretary acts on an ART request); Part 6: ss 211-219, 223, 224, 233; ART: ss 176, 181, 182, 183. Out: debts themselves (1991 Act Chapter 5); ss 191, 195(1), (3)-(3B), 198(1); ss 199-200 (end-of-employment statements); confidentiality (ss 201-210); Part 6 Divisions 4 and 5 except s 233; ss 165A, 166(1)-(2), 168, 177 (the ART's own powers and duties); ss 147A-147C and 148 (ART Act provisions switched off or modified for ART review; a finding in NOTES.md, no question to ask); s 238; Part 7 machinery.
seat: the person paid: the person who claims, receives or has received a social security payment and is told they were overpaid, is asked to explain their income, or is accused of an offence
